title: A Phase 1/2a Clinical Study of KL002 in Treatment of Parkinson's Disease
official: A Phase 1/2a, Open-Label, Single Ascending Dose Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, and Preliminary Efficacy of KL002, an AAV9 Gene Therapy, in Subjects With Parkinson's Disease
summary: To assess the safety and tolerability of single doses of KL002 over 78 weeks in subjects with Parkinson's disease。

interventions.name: Injecting KL002 into the bilateral putamen

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Males or females ≥ 40 and ≤ 75 years old
2. Diagnosis of Parkinson's disease per UK Parkinson's Disease Society Brain Bank Clinical Diagnostic Criteria
3. Duration of Parkinson's disease motor symptoms: 3-12 years
4. Hoehn and Yahr Stage II-IV (as determined in Practically Defined OFF state)
5. The OFF period MDS-UPDRS III score \> 30 ， and the percent improvement in MDS-UPDRS III in the levodopa/carbidopa challenge test is ≥ 30%
6. Must have been on a stable regimen of Parkinson's disease symptomatic therapy for at least 4 weeks prior to KL002 administration, and must remain stable through dosing unless otherwise approved by the Medical Monitor
7. Must agree to postpone any Parkinson's disease-related neurological surgery, including deep brain stimulation, until after completing the 24-month follow-up
8. Patient has the ability to understand the purpose and risks of the study and provide written informed consent and authorization to use protected health information in accordance with national and local privacy regulations

Exclusion Criteria:

1. The diagnosis of a significant central nervous system (CNS) disease other than Parkinson's disease that may be a cause for the patient's Parkinson's disease symptoms or may confound study objectives
2. Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score of \< 24
3. Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD) score of \> 17
4. Hypersensitivity or contraindications to corticosteroid use
5. History of previous brain surgery for Parkinson's disease, such as deep brain stimulation or focused ultrasound
6. Clinically significant abnormalities in laboratory test results at screening
7. Atypical Parkinson's disease or secondary Parkinson's disease caused by factors such as chemicals or toxins
8. Use of ambroxol within 8 weeks of dosing
9. Any type of prior gene or cell therapy
10. Contraindications to general anesthesia
11. Any factors that may cause the subject to be unable to follow the study protocol, including medical or social factors, or geographical inconvenience
